analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.5.26
key_insights: Futures are roughly unchanged to start the week (Nasdaq -15bps, Russell +15bps) after NDX closed at a new all-time high on Friday. 10yr yields are unchanged and WTI is down about 1%.

Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal. The note cites both a $23.7bn takeout bid and about $22.6bn in separate sections. PTC is +36% pre-market, with ADSK +5% and PCOR +6% in sympathy.
INTC is -4% and TSM +2% after Elon Musk's Terafab confirmed talks with TSMC. A Culpium newsletter says TSMC may use Terafab as anchor client for a future Texas fab. Musk called it 'just discussions'.

GS semiconductor 3Q preview: the sector pulled back over two months on de-risking (SOX -11% vs SPX +4%), and GS sees upside to estimates across most sub-sectors. It expects positive revisions for SemiCap on WFE pull-ins, upside for server CPUs and ASIC programs on higher hyperscaler capex, and favors analog with industrial, aero/defense and datacenter exposure.
GS tactical semis ideas: upside for AMAT, STX and MCHP, downside for QCOM, KLAC and WDC. In memory/storage it prefers HDDs and NAND because there are no near-term supply additions.

Prime Services: US fundamental L/S net leverage fell for a third week to 46.4%, the lowest since April 2025 and near the 2nd percentile of five-year lows. US equities were modestly net bought on short covering in Macro Products, partly offset by single-stock shorting. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold and Health Care was the most net bought.

Asset managers and hedge funds were balanced last week with more demand in semis after MU earnings and the NVDA buyback increase. The desk sees minimal willingness to chase the move higher despite light positioning.

Russell 2000 futures positioning is deeply depressed, with GS estimating systematic exposure in the 7th percentile and record leveraged-fund shorts per CFTC data as of 9/22. Softer PCE and NFP data pushed 30bp of cuts into pricing through year-end and triggered short covering, but a durable rally needs sustained relief in rates.
Derivatives desk likes IWM and QQQ upside into Q3 earnings and midterms. It traded over 140mm of NDX Dec26 105%/115% up-and-out calls and also likes NDX over RTY outperformance and NDX upvar.

ETF flows: SPX is on track to beat RTY for 7 straight weeks, the longest streak since 2018. Cybersecurity ETFs are on track for one of their best monthly inflows (+$950mm). TLT hit an all-time low and is on a 7-session losing streak.

Baskets: the softer payroll print lowered yields without raising recession fears. The desk sees room for a catch-up rally from laggards given weak breadth and light positioning, and points to GSPUBETA for high-beta upside and GSPUBETX to hedge beta ex-AI.

TMT specialists: semis regained footing (SOX +4% vs NDX +70bps) while investors saw 'wrong-way' reactions to earnings (ACN up, muted MU, JBL fade). NDX 12m forward multiple is below its multi-year average, but investors question when multiple compression ends and belief in 2027-2028 returns.

GS Q3 earnings season preview: season starts the week of October 12, and about 70% of S&P 500 market cap reports by end of October. Consensus expects 27% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3 (Q2 realized 33%). AI infrastructure beneficiaries are over 50% of EPS growth, and median-stock growth is expected to slow from 14% to 9%.

Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated to 48% last quarter and GS equity analysts expect 55% in Q3. Tariff refunds were $77bn in Q2 and $69bn in Q3, about 6% of US corporate pre-tax profits each quarter.

SIA data: IC unit shipments ex-memory rose about 2% m/m in August, better than seasonal. Shipments run 10% above long-term demand on a three-month basis (7% in July), and analog is also about 10% above trend. MCU units were 21.3% below trend, which GS attributes to consumer electronics softness.

STX and WDC fell 10%-11% Friday on reports that Toshiba aims to double nearline HDD capacity by end of FY27 versus FY25, with a roughly ¥60bn Philippines investment. Toshiba also targets 30% HDD share (from about 11%) and 65TB drives in 2030, which would match Seagate and Western Digital's roadmaps at face value.

GS maintains Sell on Adobe ahead of the 12/1 CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy. It sees the new leadership as a possible catalyst but wants visibility into strategic decisions while competition intensifies.

GS upgrades Z.AI (Zhipu) to Buy from Neutral with a HK$1,560 target (prior HK$1,610) on raised 2026E year-end ARR of US$3.2bn (prior US$2.7bn). The stock is down 70% since July at a sub-US$40bn market cap, and GS cites dilution from c.US$9bn of equity raisings and pre-IPO share unlocks from early January 2027 as risks.

Macro: 2yr 4.80%, 10yr 5.27%, 30yr 5.625%, WTI $90.80. Weekend headlines were a Yemen government campaign against Houthi-held territory, French and Spanish political and fiscal stress with the euro at a 17-month low, and Brazil's election (EWZ +13% pre-market).

Calendar: ISM Services today (GS 55.4, consensus 55.0), FOMC minutes Wednesday, U of Mich Friday. Earnings: STZ Tuesday night, APLD Wednesday night, PEP Thursday morning, DAL Friday morning. MRVL and ZS hold investor days Tuesday.

Hyperscaler cloud revenue growth was 48% in Q2 (reported). GS equity analysts estimate 55% in Q3. Analyst estimates show hyperscaler capex growth of 116% and AI infrastructure beneficiaries above 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth.
